neighbours.label: the subject pronoun of a comparison clause after 'like' or 'as' ('like they do on a windshield', 'much as it did')
fire: The new phone handles photos much as it did before the update.
Our dog guards the garden just like it guards the front door.
The children cleaned their rooms like they clean the classroom at school.
The river floods the meadow every spring, as it has for centuries.
My parents still argue about money like they did when I was small.
The old printer jams on thick paper, just as it always has.
The players celebrated the draw like they had won the cup.
The software sorts the files much as it sorts the emails.
quiet: The new phone handles photos well, and it did so before the update too.
Our dog guards the garden, and it barks at every stranger.
The children cleaned their rooms because they wanted to go outside.
The river floods the meadow every spring, and it ruins the hay.
My parents still argue about money, but they always make up.
The old printer jams on thick paper, so it sits unused in the corner.
The players celebrated the draw although they had hoped to win.
The software sorts the files, then it backs up the emails.
